web_evidence.title: Tara Conklin with Wendy Hinman — Writers Connection
web_evidence.note: In a direct author interview, Conklin identifies Fiona as the overarching narrator but says she adopted various POV characters to tell the siblings' experiences intimately, establishing the novel-wide mixed structure.

web_evidence.title: The Last Romantics: A Novel — Chapter 1
web_evidence.note: The licensed sustained opening begins with story-specific first-person plural narration about 'our father' and 'we lived,' then includes Fiona's singular 'my father,' confirming the participating Fiona strand.

web_evidence.title: Review: The Last Romantics by Tara Conklin — BookNAround
web_evidence.note: The reviewer explicitly reports that Fiona narrates most of the story in first person and that narration occasionally shifts to third person for the other siblings.

web_evidence.title: The Last Romantics Book Club Service — Geneva Public Library District
web_evidence.note: This library-hosted guide reproduces professional Library Journal and Kirkus structural assessments: Fiona is the narrator, while the narrative also enters siblings' private thoughts that she could not know, corroborating the distinct close/omniscient passages visible in the quotes.

web_evidence.title: The Last Romantics by Tara Conklin — Publishers Weekly
web_evidence.note: The professional review calls Fiona the novel's key voice while noting that the narrative expands into the minds of the other family members, corroborating the mixed-person structure.

person_note: The novel sustains more than one base-narration person. Fiona, a Skinner sibling, is the overarching participating narrator: the quotes repeatedly use story-specific I, my, we, our, and us, and the licensed opening independently confirms that first-person strand. Other passages give close third-person access to Renee, Caroline, and other siblings. Conklin's direct structural explanation, a library-hosted guide, and explicit whole-book reviews show that these are adopted sibling POV passages rather than merely Fiona mentioning relatives. Accordingly the book is ALTERNATING, with a predominant first-person Fiona frame and sustained third-person sibling sections. Generic 'you' aphorisms and direct address are local gnomic or dialogue material, not a second-person strand. Confidence is medium because the collection-level structural evidence is Tier C despite the repeated quote pattern.
